newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco firms will contest FDA factual assertions.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco firms will contest FDA factual assertions.

text.p: Tobacco companies, responding to a federal court ruling allowing limited Food and Drug Administration regulation of the tobacco industry, said Friday that as the case proceeds they will challenge factual assertions in FDA regulations.
U.S. District Judge William Osteen ruled today that the FDA can regulate sales and labeling of cigarettes but not the promotion and advertising of tobacco products.

The tobacco companies, in a joint statement, said the court concluded that Congress did not expressly prohibit the FDA from regulating tobacco products under existing laws if the factual assertions in FDA regulations are proven to be correct.
The court said the industry was free to contest those factual assertions, and the industry will do just that, the companies said.
They also said the court did not decide the constitutional challenges to the proposed FDA regulations raised by the industry and advertisers.
The court ruled only that the FDA does not have authority under food and drug laws to regulate tobacco advertising and promotion, they said.

Industry sources said FDA assertions that might be challenged by the industry include allegations that tobacco companies market their products to children and manipulate nicotine levels in cigarettes.

The regulatory battle dates to August 1995, when President Clinton authorized the FDA to regulate how cigarettes are sold and marketed, in a bid to curb smoking by children. Some of the FDA rules took effect in February; others were to take effect later this year.
Today's ruling comes amid growing pressure on cigarette makers to settle lawsuits seeking billions of dollars for smoking-related illnesses.
